title: Selling to Non-linear Agents: A Demand-Based Auction
abstract: arXiv:2003.00545v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Auctions allocate scarce goods, from car licenses to online advertising, to buyers whose utilities are often not linear in money, as with budgets or risk aversion. We ask how a seller should sell to such buyers and what learning their preferences is worth. We propose demand-based auctions, which elicit demand curves and are dominant-strategy incentive compatible for any non-linear utilities. The revenue-maximizing one takes familiar second-price forms and is max-min optimal when the seller observes only demand curves. Under standard assumptions, learning risk attitudes beyond demand curves adds relatively little revenue, as does learning budgets unless they correlate with values.

translated_title: 向非线性代理人销售：一种基于需求的拍卖
translated_abstract: 拍卖将稀缺商品（从车牌到在线广告）分配给买家，而这些买家的效用通常不是货币的线性函数，例如存在预算约束或风险厌恶的情况。我们探讨卖家应如何向这类买家销售，以及了解其偏好究竟价值几何。我们提出了基于需求的拍卖机制，该机制通过引出需求曲线，对任意非线性效用均满足占优策略激励相容。其中收益最大化的形式采用了人们熟悉的第二价格拍卖形式，并且当卖家仅能观察需求曲线时是最小最大最优的。在标准假设下，除需求曲线之外再学习买家的风险态度所带来的收益提升相对有限；除非预算与估值相关，否则学习预算信息同样如此。
tldr: 提出了基于需求的拍卖机制，该机制通过引出需求曲线对任意非线性效用实现占优策略激励相容，其收益最大化形式具有第二价格拍卖的形式且在卖家仅观察需求曲线时是最小最大最优的，同时证明在标准假设下学习需求曲线之外的风险态度或预算信息带来的额外收益有限。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes demand-based auctions that elicit demand curves and achieve dominant-strategy incentive compatibility for any non-linear utilities, with the revenue-maximizing version taking a familiar second-price form and being max-min optimal when the seller observes only demand curves, further showing that learning preferences beyond demand curves adds relatively little revenue under standard assumptions.
